audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL gas economics (EIP-3651 warm COINBASE, EIP-7691 blob gas pricing), CL-to-EL withdrawal processing (EIP-4895), EVM INVALID opcode (EIP-141), P2P fork compatibility (EIP-6122), state recovery proposals (EIP-867), SHA256 precompile execution, execution proof generation and relay (EIP-8025), transaction/block validation exception handling, and P2P client identity disclosure (EIP-7636).

out_of_scope: Full EVM opcode set beyond covered EIPs

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, exploit warm COINBASE for gas manipulation, craft transactions targeting INVALID opcode edge cases, submit blob transactions exceeding limits
Send invalid blocks, eclipse attacks, send blocks with invalid withdrawal roots, propagate blocks with incorrect blob counts
Exploit SHA256 precompile gas underpricing for DoS, use INVALID opcode to waste gas, manipulate COINBASE payment patterns

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid withdrawals, manipulate withdrawal ordering, include excessive blobs, forge execution proofs

cl_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (proof engine REST, MEV-Boost relay)
cl_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect execution proofs, manipulate proof generation, denial of service on proof engine
Send incompatible ForkIDs to partition network, spoof client identity in ENR records, submit forged signed execution proofs

misclassified_entities.reason: Contract logic triggering INVALID opcode is an internal EVM execution component, not an external entity sending data from outside the system boundary.
The withdrawal processing system is an internal EL component that iterates through withdrawals in the payload, not an external entity.
A smart contract invoking SHA256 precompile is an internal EVM execution path, not an external entity crossing the system boundary.
Labeled as external but actually represents data flowing within the EVM from internal contract calls to precompiles. The true external entity is the original transaction submitter.
Chain configuration is a local trusted configuration source, not an external entity sending data into the system from outside.
Node operator is a local trusted administrator, not an external entity interacting with the system over a network boundary.
Generic 'Transaction' entity in EIP-141 is too vague; the actual external entity is the transaction submitter via JSON-RPC or P2P.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC endpoint. Users submit transactions that trigger EIP-3651 access list initialization, INVALID opcode execution, SHA256 precompile calls, and blob transactions. All input must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. CL provides withdrawal lists (EIP-4895), execution payloads with blob data, and block parameters. Content must still be validated: withdrawal roots, blob gas, blob counts.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peer proposing blocks. Blocks may contain invalid withdrawal commitments (EIP-4895), incorrect blob counts (EIP-7691), or malformed state transitions. Full validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (devp2p/discv5)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P handshake (ForkID exchange, ENR records, block relay)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer. Sends ForkIDs for compatibility checking (EIP-6122), ENR records with self-reported client info (EIP-7636), and blocks for validation. All data potentially malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via CL Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CL P2P gossip (signed execution proofs, ENR)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated CL gossip network peer. May submit forged execution proofs (EIP-8025), falsified client identity ENR entries (EIP-7636), or incompatible ForkIDs. Requires BLS signature verification and whitelist checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Proof Engine via REST API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Local service authenticated implicitly via localhost access. Generates execution proofs (EIP-8025). Content requires verification since a compromised proof engine could produce invalid proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Proof Submitter via Gossip Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any network participant claiming to be a prover. Must be verified against prover whitelist, BLS signature validated, proof data checked non-empty, and duplicates rejected (EIP-8025).

trusted_external_entities.name: Filesystem (SCO Files) via local storage
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SCO files loaded from filesystem could be tampered with by attacker with local access. Scripts must be audited for unsafe operations, block heights must be hardcoded, and no unlocked wallets should be used during verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Validator via CL Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain withdrawal queue, block proposals
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit withdrawal requests and propose blocks. While validators are staked, they may still be malicious. Withdrawal data requires validation by CL before passing to EL (EIP-4895).

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce checking, gas limit validation, intrinsic gas coverage, sender balance check, blob count limits. Transactions trigger EIP-3651 COINBASE warming, may invoke SHA256 precompile, and may hit INVALID opcode.

Withdrawal list content must be validated: compute withdrawals trie root and verify against header withdrawals_root. Amount conversion from Gwei to Wei must be checked for overflow. Blob gas parameters must match EIP-7691 limits.

Full block validation: withdrawals_root commitment verification, blob count <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA (9), blob gas <= MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (1,179,648), all transactions valid, state transitions correct.
ForkID must be validated against local chain configuration. Stale peers must be rejected. Incompatible fork configurations must cause disconnection. CRC32 collision resistance assumed sufficient.
Client identity data is self-reported and MUST NOT be used for security-critical decisions. RLP decoding and ASCII validation required. Data may only be used for non-critical analytics.
Full block validation required including InvalidBlock exception handling, transaction validation (nonce, signature, gas, balance), and state integrity checks (no empty accounts in state).

Proof validation pipeline: verify proof_data non-empty, cryptographic proof verification via proof engine, duplicate detection, prover pubkey whitelist check, BLS signature verification using DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF.

Proof content must be validated even from semi-trusted local engine. Proof data should be non-empty, proof_gen_id should be tracked, and the resulting proof must pass independent verification before signing and broadcast.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: SCO file loading at client startup (EIP-867)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: SCO files must be audited: verification scripts checked for unsafe operations, target block heights must be hardcoded, no unlocked wallets during verification, expected code hashes validated before state changes.

Validator withdrawal requests must be validated by CL: validator index verified, withdrawal address confirmed, amount within expected bounds, monotonically increasing index assigned. Bounded quantity per block enforced.
